en.title: Getting lost and getting help
en.summary: What to say when you do not know where you are, and how to follow a sequence of directions.

paragraphs: Getting lost is part of travelling. In this lesson you will learn to explain your problem, to ask for help and to follow directions step by step.
Grace cannot find her hotel and calls her friend Ben, who is waiting there.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Hello, Ben. I am lost. I cannot find the hotel.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I am on a street called Mill Road, but I do not know which way to go.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Is there a shop or a sign nearby?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: There is a chemist on the corner and a bus stop opposite.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Good. Walk back to the main road, then turn left. Go past the church and take the second street on the right.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Could you repeat that, please? You were going too fast.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Of course. Main road, turn left, past the church, second right. The hotel is on your left.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Got it. I will be there in ten minutes.

paragraphs: **1. Can and cannot show what you are able to do.** Use cannot (can't) with the base verb to name a problem, and could to ask for help politely. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
FunctionExample
problemI can't find the hotel.
polite requestCould you repeat that, please?
offerCan I help you?
request for speedCould you speak more slowly?

paragraphs: **2. Sequence words order the directions.** First, then, after that and finally tell the listener which step comes next, and the imperative gives each step. See Introduction to Grammar: Adverbs.

blocks.html:
WordExample
firstFirst, walk back to the main road.
thenThen turn left.
after thatAfter that, go past the church.
finallyFinally, take the second street.

items: I am lost means you do not know where you are.
A person is lost, but an object is missing.
Take the second street means count the streets and turn at the second.
In an emergency, call 999 in Britain or 911 in the United States.

paragraphs: A phone map is useful, but English speakers are not shy about being asked for directions. A polite opening such as Excuse me, I am a little lost, can you help? usually brings a friendly answer.
